item.text: I’ve already cleaned up the main implementation once, so I’m checking the current state to see whether there’s still meaningful refactor work left. If there is, I’ll carry it through rather than just restating the last change.

There’s still a worthwhile refactor here: the utility is solving an array problem through boxed `List<Integer>` values and mixes formatting directly into `main`. I’m tightening that into a primitive-array API and a separate formatting path so the code better matches the problem domain.
The implementation now stays on primitive arrays end to end and no longer couples output formatting to the accumulation loop. I’m compiling and running it again to confirm the behavior is unchanged.

Refactored [PrefixSum.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/003_prefix_sum_array/PrefixSum.java:1) further so the API now matches the problem domain.

`build(...)` now returns `int[]` instead of `List<Integer>`, which removes boxing overhead and keeps the implementation array-based throughout. I also split output concerns into a separate `format(...)` method, so prefix-sum calculation and presentation are no longer mixed in `main`.
